new_statements.quote: p. 24 (section I.1.3 'Les tons'; PDF p. 34): "A propos des tons dans la langue tukí, ESSONO (1980 : 20) déclare : «Comme toutes les langues bantoues du Cameroun, le tukí est une langue à ton.» Par la suite, il dénombre 5 tons phonétiques du tùkí dont trois tons simples ( haut, bas et moyen ) et deux tons modulés, dérivants des combinaisons des tons haut et bas. [...] En dehors du ton moyen, tous les autres tons du tukí ont un statut phonologique et remplissent une fonction lexicale et une fonction grammaticale." p. 25 (PDF p. 35): "Ainsi, les tonèmes du tukí se résument en deux tons ponctuels dont un ton haut ( ́) et un ton bas ( ̀), deux tons modulés dont un ton bas-haut ( ̌ ) et un ton haut-bas ( ̂ )."
new_statements.translation: p. 24: "Concerning the tones of the Tuki language, ESSONO (1980: 20) states: 'Like all the Bantu languages of Cameroon, Tuki is a tone language.' He then counts 5 phonetic tones in Tuki, three simple tones (high, low and mid) and two contour tones deriving from combinations of the high and low tones. [...] Apart from the mid tone, all the other tones of Tuki have phonological status and fulfil a lexical function and a grammatical function." p. 25: "Thus the tonemes of Tuki come down to two level tones, a high tone and a low tone, and two contour tones, a low-high (rising) tone and a high-low (falling) tone."
new_statements.citation: Kongne Welaze, Jacquis. 2004. Morphologie verbale du tukí. Mémoire, Université de Yaoundé I. x+113 pp.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-opened the mirror copy (4,070,909 bytes, the PDF's metadata: 123 pp., Acrobat Capture 3.0, created 2005-12-16.) and its extracted text. On the identity of the variety: one slotted page render render of p. 1 (100 dpi, deleted afterwards) shows the title page 'UNIVERSITE DE YAOUNDE I.. DEPARTEMENT DE LANGUES AFRICAINES ET LINGUISTIQUE / MORPHOLOGIE VERBALE DU tuki / Memoire presente et soutenu en vue de l'obtention du Diplome de Maitrise en Linguistique Generale / Par Jacquis KONGNE WELAZE / Sous la direction de Dr Zachee Denis BITJAA KODY / Annee academique 2003-2004' = the cited 2004 Yaounde I memoire; the saved PuRe record (work folder) reads title 'Morphologie verbale du tuki', creator…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record. The language has no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project; this first-hand source adds only a tone statement (Tuki is a tone language, H/L tonemes + contours) and is silent on word stress, consistent with the four sources already read ('silent on stress': Hyman & Biloa 1992, Précis d'orthographe 2008, PHOIBLE 1573, Wikipedia/Glottolog/Grambank). PHOIBLE inventory 1573 is sourced from this very mémoire (phoible_inventoryid 1573 in Glottolog 68924).
new_statements.rule_in_words: The mémoire treats Tuki (Tutsingo variety) as a tone language: two level tonemes H and L with lexical and grammatical function, plus rising and falling contours analysed over morae; a surface mid tone arises from lowering of a final H in H-L-H (Tutsingo realises H-L-M rather than Essono's H-M-M terracing); low tone is left unmarked in the transcription; verb suffixes are underlyingly L and receive H by high-tone spreading from the radical (II.1.3 'Règle tonale', p. 31-32); a floating H pre-initial causes tone raising and downstep in negative forms (IV.1.1, p. 62-63). The only suprasegmental section is I.1.3 'Les tons' (p. 24-25); the words accent/stress/accent tonique/intensité do not occur anywhere in the 123-page text, and nothing is said about word stress, prominence or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: none regarding stress; tonal detail only (mid tone non-phonemic, derived by lowering of final H after L in Tutsingo)
new_statements.identity_note: The mémoire describes the tútsíŋgó (Tutsingo / Tsinga) variety of Tuki (bag, A601), data from speakers of the villages Nyamanga II, Enangana and Bilomo collected 2002-2004 under the ANACLAC BASAL-tuki project (p. 15); it notes that Tutsingo realises H-L-H as H-L-M, differing from Essono's (1974, 1980) description of tonal terracing for the Ati/Sanaga variety.

sources.citation: Kongne Welaze, Jacquis, Ginger Boyd, Marguerite Biteya & Gabriel Okalia. 2008. Précis d'orthographe pour la langue tuki. Yaoundé: Centre ANACLAC de Linguistique Appliquée (CLA). 17 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. §3 'Les tons' (pp. 7-9): 'Nous avons identifié 5 tons de surface en tuki : 3 tons ponctuels, haut [á], moyen [ā] et bas [à]; et 2 tons modulés, montant [ǎ] et descendant [â]'; mid tones derive from downstepped H; contour tones only on long vowels; lexical minimal pairs for tone; no grammatical meaning carried by tone alone. Consonant/vowel/tone/word-division sections only.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. & Edmond Biloa. 1992. Transparent Low Tone in Tuki. Proceedings of the Eighteenth Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society: Special Session on the Typology of Tone Languages, 104-127. doi:10.3765/bls.v18i2.1547
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2 'Tuki tonology' (p. 105) gives the tone system of the Kombe dialect: surface H, L and downstepped !H; HL falling tones occur, LH rising rare; only vowels (moras) bear tone; vowel-length contrast, CVV = two moras. The word 'accent' appears only in the introduction (p. 104) about tone attraction to a designated mora in OTHER Bantu languages; no word-stress statement for Tuki.
Segment inventory (39 segments) with tone segments ˦, ˨, ˦˨, ˨˦; nothing on stress.
